newsitem.title: USA: Applied Power unit wins Northwest Air order.
newsitem.headline: Applied Power unit wins Northwest Air order.

text.p: Applied Power Inc said Wednesday its Barry Controls Aerospace unit won a contract from Northwest Airlines Corp to install its engine noise suppressor system on the carrier's planes.

The so-called Active Tuned Mass Absorber (ATMA) system is expected to be installed on Northwest's entire fleet of McDonnell Douglas Corp DC-9 aircraft by mid-1998, Applied Power said. The system, which reduces noise in all engine settings, requires no modifications or additions to the interior of the airliner.
Financial terms of the contract were not announced.
Applied Power provides engineering services to a variety of industries.
Its shares were unchanged Wednesday at 42-1/4.
